bullets.text: The meteorological department warns of heavy thunderstorms in Chennai over the next three hours, requiring the office to monitor weather alerts closely.
Heavy rains lashed Chennai and its suburbs overnight, and the office should watch for waterlogging reports across the city.
The Greater Chennai Corporation has repaired 1,531 of 13,227 rain-damaged potholes, and the office must track ongoing road restoration progress.
Chennai faces air quality monitoring issues ahead of Diwali as sensors fail, prompting the office to watch for AQI updates.
Tiruttani Murugan Temple in Thiruvallur district has announced darshan time restrictions for the Kandha Sashti festival starting November 10, so the office should monitor crowd management.
The Bharat Summit 2026 in Hyderabad will bring 450 delegates from 100 countries to discuss AI and urbanisation, and our office should observe related technological outcomes.

takeaways: Chennai citizens lack reliable air quality data as state monitors fail and sensors go blank.
The 62 crore sensor network malfunction leaves residents blind during Diwali firecracker smoke.
